title: Platform systems & services 14 how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, retrospectives and roadmap (Q3 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates the primary platform systems & services guidance for the Platform team: service inventory and owners, standard Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alerting conventions, operational runbooks for common incidents, retrospective learnings from recent incidents, and the roadmap for Q2
ToQ4 2026. It is intended for on-call engineers, platform SREs, and component owners.

Scope & audience
----------------
- Audience: platform on-call, platform engineers, infra SREs, platform product managers.
- Scope: systems supporting inference routing, batching, KV cache, telemetry, and the platform control plane (hosted & dedicated). Not a developer SDK guide.

Systems & services inventory (high level)
----------------------------------------
Below are the primary platform services, owners, and the service-level objectives (SLOs) we operate against. These are the canonical owner contacts and SLOs used in alert routing and runbooks.

Service | Primary owner | PagerDuty escalation | SLO (global)
------|---------------|----------------------|-------------
platform-api | @aisha.patel | PD:platform-api-prod | availability 99.9% monthly
model-router | @diego.ramirez | PD:model-router | p95 request latency < 250ms
batcher | @evan.thompson | PD:batcher | queueing latency p95 < 150ms
kv-cache | @liam.chen | PD:kv-cache | cache hit rate >= 85%
observability-ingest | @priya.nair | PD:obs-ingest | telemetry delivery >= 99%
storage-mgmt | @maria-gonzalez | PD:storage | disk utilization < 80% per host

Notes:
- Ownership is authoritative for escalation and runbook triage. If the contact is unavailable, follow the PagerDuty escalation policy listed.
- SLOs above are for production clusters (hosted and dedicated). Private deployments may have different contractual SLOs; see customer-specific runbooks under eng-private-deployments.

Dashboards & alerts (standards)
--------------------------------
Recommended dashboards (Grafana):
- Platform / Overview (grafana id: grafana::dash-1001) — global traffic, token rate, error rates, model-selector heatmap.
- Routing / Model-router (grafana id: grafana::dash-1102) — p50/p95/p99 latencies, active connections, slow-model histogram.
- Batcher / Queueing (grafana id: grafana::dash-1203) — inflight batch size, batch latency distribution, backpressure events.
- KV cache (grafana id: grafana::dash-1304) — hit rate, miss reasons, mem usage per host.
- Observability Ingest (grafana id: grafana::dash-1405) — ingestion rate, dropped spans, prometheus remote_write failures.

Alert naming convention
- Format: team.service.condition. Example: platform.model-router.latency_p95_gt_250ms
- Every alert must include: severity (critical/warning), runbook link, PagerDuty schedule.

Typical Prometheus alert examples (copy into prometheus/rules/platform.rules.yml):
```
groups:
- name: platform-latency
  rules:
  - alert: ModelRouterLatencyP95High
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(model_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,instance)) > 0.25
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: critical
      team: platform
    annotations:
      summary: "model-router p95 latency > 250ms"
      runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/platform-model-router-latency-runbook"
```

Alert thresholds (standard):
- Critical: error_rate > 1% for 5m OR p95 latency > configured SLO for 5m OR ingestion failure rate > 0.5% for 15m.
- Warning: error_rate > 0.5% for 10m OR p95 latency > 80% of SLO for 10m.

PagerDuty mappings (example)
- PD:platform-api -> escalation policy: Platform Production -> primary on-call (1st) -> platform lead (2nd) -> eng-sre (3rd).
- PD:model-router -> Model Router squad schedule.
(See PagerDuty console for live mapping.)

How-tos (common procedures)
---------------------------
1) Create a new Grafana panel and alert
   - Navigate to the Grafana dashboard namespace -> select dashboard -> Edit.
   - Add query (PromQL), set visualization -> save with version notes.
   - For alerts, create a Prometheus rule in platform.rules.yml and submit a PR to infra-monitoring. Example PR title: "infra-monitoring: add alert model-router p95 > 250ms".
   - Link the runbook in the alert annotation: runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/<<runbook-page>>".

2) Add a service to platform service discovery
   - Commit service registration to infra/consul/services/platform-services.yaml with fields: name, owner, health_check, metrics_endpoint.
   - Run: `make svc-register SERVICE=name ENV=prod` on the infra repo.
   - Verify: `curl -s https://consul-internal/api/v1/health/service/name` and confirm nodes report passing.

3) Deploy a Prometheus rule change (safe flow)
   - Fork infra-monitoring -> add rule -> run unit tests (`make test-rules`).
   - Open PR, request review from observability lead (@priya.nair).
   - After merge, run `kubectl rollout restart deploy/prometheus` in monitoring namespace. Monitor for false positives for 30 minutes.

Operational runbooks (playbook excerpts)
--------------------------------------
A. High aggregate latency (Model-router critical latency)
1) Triage
   - Check Grafana dashboard grafana::dash-1102 for p50/p95/p99 and per-model breakdown.
   - Confirm alert details in Prometheus -> alert history -> annotation runbook link.
2) Immediate mitigation (if production impact)
   - If a specific model is slow, add a routing override to fallback to compatible, lower-latency variant: `rbacctl patch /routing/overrides --payload '{\"model\":\"gpt-3.5-mini\",\"reason\":\"auto-fallback\"}'` (internal CLI).
   - Increase batcher concurrency temporarily: `kubectl scale deploy/batcher --replicas=<+2>` (ensure capacity in GPU pool).
3) Root cause & recovery
   - Check model-node hot metrics (GPU utilization, OOMs, kernel failures).
   - If a node shows OOM or CUDA driver errors, cordon + drain and restart pods; follow host runbook: "/confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/host-restart-runbook".
4) Post-incident
   - File an incident postmortem (use incident template under oncall-and-incident-response/game-days).

B. Observability ingest drop (telemetry not arriving)
1) Triage
   - Check remote_write and agent logs (observability-ingest).
   - Query: `sum(rate(prometheus_agent_push_errors_total[5m])) by (instance)`
2) Mitigation
   - Restart ingesters: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/obs-ingester -n monitoring` one pod at a time.
   - If Prometheus remote_write endpoint is rate-limited, add temporary backpressure by pausing low-priority telemetry exporters: `kubectl scale deploy/dev-exporter --replicas=0 -n staging`.
3) Recovery & RCA
   - Reconcile missing telemetry by replaying ingestion from kafka topic `telemetry-replay` (see obs-playbook for replay CLI).

C. Disk pressure on storage-mgmt hosts
1) Triage
   - Check `node_filesystem_avail_bytes` and `node_filesystem_avail_bytes / node_filesystem_size_bytes` for hosts with <20% free.
2) Mitigation
   - Evacuate non-critical workloads: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and migrate storage shards.
   - Trigger cleanup job: `kubectl run cleanup-disk --image=company/cleanup:latest -- /bin/clean-temp` with safe mode first.
3) Recovery
   - Increase filesystem capacity (resize LVM or attach new disk) and uncordon.

Runbook checklist for on-call responders
- Acknowledge the PD alert within 5 minutes.
- Post status to #platform-incident Slack channel with incident-id and summary.
- Follow mitigation steps in this document.
- If mitigation fails after 20 minutes, escalate to the secondary on-call and platform lead.

Retrospective summary (last quarter)
-----------------------------------
Incidents of note:
- MR-2026-02: Model-router latency spike (2026-02-10) — root cause: misconfigured kernel compilation on a recent host image that changed scheduling behavior. Mitigation: rollback image and pin kernel flags. Action item: add kernel smoke tests to GPU fleet CI (owner: eng-infra, due 2026-04-15).
- OBS-2026-01: Observability ingest drop (2026-01-22) — root cause: Prometheus remote_write timeout due to bursting traffic from a new customer pipeline. Mitigation: added rate-limiting and backpressure. Action item: provide per-customer throttling controls and integration test (owner: observability, due 2026-05-01).

Blameless action items (status):
- Kernel smoke tests for GPU fleet CI (owner: eng-infra) — in_progress.
- Add per-customer telemetry QoS (owner: observability) — in_progress.
- Dashboard coverage gap: add SLI panel for per-model tail-latency (owner: platform) — planned for Q3.

Roadmap (Q2
ToQ4 2026)
--------------------
Q2 2026 (near-term):
- Standardize dashboard library and templating across clusters (owner: platform-observability).
- Audit all alerts for runbook links and owner fields (owner: eng-sre).

Q3 2026 (current cycle):
- Per-model tail-latency observability: add per-model p99 heatmaps and automated anomaly detection (owner: platform, target: 2026-09-15).
- Batcher autoscaling alpha: improved autoscaling policy based on token backlog (owner: batcher, target: 2026-09-30).
- Runbook automation: wire common mitigation steps into /infra/runbook-automation (owner: eng-platform, target: 2026-10-15).

Q4 2026 (planning):
- Cross-region failover runbooks and drills for multi-region routing (owner: eng-sre, target: 2026-12-15).
- Observability retention review and cost optimization (owner: finance + observability).

------------------------------
- Platform team wiki home: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026.json
- On-call playbook quick start: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Monitoring & alerting standards: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards
- Private deployment runbooks: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops

Appendices
----------
A. Common Prometheus queries
- p95 request latency (model-router): `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(model_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))`
- error rate: `sum(rate(model_request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(model_request_total[5m]))`

B. Useful CLI snippets
- Check service health (consul): `curl -s https://consul-internal/api/v1/health/service/model-router | jq .`
- Restarting a deployment safely: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-router -n platform --timeout=10m`

C. Contacts
- Platform lead: Aisha Patel (@aisha.patel) — aisha@redwood-inference.com
- Observability lead: Priya Nair (@priya.nair)
- Eng SRE on-call: see PagerDuty schedule

If anything in this doc conflicts with team-specific runbooks, follow the team-specific runbooks and notify document owners to reconcile. For edits: open a PR against the confluence source and request at least one reviewer from the reviewers list above.
